content:
Apple's iPhone lineup this fall is reportedly set to revolve around the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra. Here are the three most important feature differences (excluding price) that could affect your upgrade decision.

Design: Traditional vs. Foldable

This difference is the most obvious, but it's worth mentioning because it's also the most important.

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will retain the same basic design language that iPhones have used for years. Their display sizes and overall design are reportedly identical to the previous generation. If you want the traditional iPhone feel, the iPhone 18 Pro will be your top pick.

As for the iPhone Ultra, it will be Apple's first foldable model. It features a distinctly different form factor, with an outer display that's shorter and wider than a traditional iPhone, and an inner display resembling an iPad mini.

Camera: Pro Will Continue to Reign Supreme

Apple has consistently reserved its most advanced and innovative camera technology for the Pro models. This year is no exception.

The iPhone Ultra is expected to feature largely the same camera setup as the iPhone 18 Pro, with one major exception: it will not include a telephoto lens.

Reports suggest the iPhone Ultra will still sport the same main lens, ultrawide lens, and front-facing camera as the Pro lineup. However, the telephoto lens will remain exclusive to the Pro models, with its performance reportedly set to improve even further this year.

Performance: Both Pack the A20 Pro Chip, but Materials Differ

Both the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra are expected to run on the A20 Pro chip at their core. However, due to differences in design and materials, real-world performance may vary.

The iPhone 18 Pro will carry over the unibody aluminum design from the iPhone 17 Pro, along with the same vapor chamber for thermal management. These two changes resulted in better overall performance compared to its predecessor, as the iPhone is able to maintain lower temperatures during demanding tasks.

As for the iPhone Ultra, it will adopt a sleek titanium design similar to that of the iPhone Air. It may also feature a vapor chamber, though only one leaker has made this claim so far. Nevertheless, due to the material differences, even with the same chip, the iPhone Ultra may still fall slightly behind the iPhone 18 Pro in performance under direct sunlight or during intensive workloads.
